words.def: A bomb is an object that explodes and destroys large areas.
words.ex: The bomb will destroy anything that is near.

words.def: A certificate is a document that says that something is true or happened.
words.ex: I was given a certificate after completing the computer course.

words.def: A circumstance is an event that makes a situation what it is.
words.ex: There were many circumstances behind their success like hard work.

words.def: A coffin is a box used to bury dead people.
words.ex: When a person passes away, they are usually buried inside of a coffin.

words.def: To cope with a difficult or stressful situation means to deal with it.
words.ex: He copes with work stress by exercising three or four times a week.

words.def: Criticism is the act of saying that you don’t like or approve of something.
words.ex: She had a lot of criticism about their new plan.

words.def: To devastate something means to completely destroy it.
words.ex: The entire wall was devastated.

words.def: To frown is to make an unhappy look with your face.
words.ex: Melissa frowned when she found out that the party had been cancelled.

words.def: To gaze at something means to look at it for a long time.
words.ex: We used a telescope to gaze at the stars for over an hour.

words.def: To glance at something means to look at it quickly.
words.ex: She glanced behind her to see if he was looking at her.

words.def: Grief is the feeling of deep sadness, usually when a person dies.
words.ex: The grief caused by losing her parents was very difficult for her.

words.def: A groom is a man who is going to be married.
words.ex: The groom looked happy as he walked with his new wife.

words.def: A license is an official document that gives one permission to do something.
words.ex: In the United States you need a driver’s license to drive legally.

words.def: A microscope is a device that makes small objects look bigger.
words.ex: Germs cannot be seen without a microscope.

words.def: When something is nuclear, it relates to the division or joining of atoms.
words.ex: Nuclear power plants provide inexpensive energy to cities.

words.def: To portray something means to describe it or show it in a picture.
words.ex: Her picture portrayed the house she grew up in when she was little.

words.def: To rotate something means to turn it around in a circle.
words.ex: An airplane’s propellers rotate quickly to help it fly.

words.def: A souvenir is something you buy to remind you of a place or event.
words.ex: I bought a Russian doll as a souvenir from my trip to Moscow.

words.def: A submarine is a boat that can go underwater for long periods of time.
words.ex: The submarine dove under the sea so the enemy couldn’t see it.

words.def: To trace something means to follow over it with the eyes or a finger.
words.ex: He traced over the graph with his finger.

story.title: An Interesting Life
paragraphs: A man looked through some boxes with his grandson. They were filled with old photographs and objects that portrayed important events from the grandfather’s life.
He wished to share the circumstances behind each event with his grandson.
The grandson, however, thought his grandfather’s stories were boring. The grandfather coped with this. He ignored his grandson’s criticism.
He took a photo from the box. “That’s the submarine I was on during the war,” he explained. The grandson gazed at it.
The grandfather glanced at the next picture and frowned. It showed a row of coffins. His grandson noticed the grief in his grandfather’s face.
“This was after a nuclear bomb was dropped,” the grandfather answered. “It devastated a city.”
Next the grandfather pulled a toy microscope from the box and rotated it in his hand.
“Where did you get that?” the grandson asked.
“This is a souvenir I bought at the science museum,” the grandfather said.
Now the boy was really interested. He started to understand that his grandfather was telling him a larger story. It was the story of his grandfather’s life.
He got another photo. It showed a young bride and groom. They were very happy. A certificate was attached to the photo. The boy couldn’t read it, but he traced his finger over paper.
“That’s my marriage license from the day I married your grandmother,” the grandfather said.
“Wow!” said the boy. “Granddad, now I know all about your life!”

story_exercise.title: Answer the questions based on the story.

questions.content: 1. Which of the following was NOT in the box?
questions.explanation: The story mentions photographs, souvenirs (toy microscope), and a marriage license, but not letters.

questions.content: 2. What did the grandfather say he did during the war?
questions.explanation: He took a photo and said, “That’s the submarine I was on during the war.”

questions.content: 3. How did the grandson feel at first about the circumstances behind each photograph?
questions.explanation: The grandson thought his grandfather's stories were boring at first.

questions.content: 4. All of the following are true about the toy microscope EXCEPT _____.
options: the grandfather rotated it in his hand
the grandson only glanced at it
the grandfather bought it at a museum
questions.correctAnswer: the grandson only glanced at it
questions.explanation: The grandson was really interested, not just glanced at it.
